subject: Post-demo: cache coverage, hit-rate scenarios & target unit economics
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Green <sophie@acmetherm.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: cache coverage, hit-rate scenarios & target unit economics

Hi Sophie / Tom —

Thanks again for carving out time today — great to see the ingestion demo and hear how the search+assistant will be used across internal ops and field techs. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the short recap and the numbers we discussed so we can align on pricing sensitivity around caching.

Quick recap of what Acme needs (from today):
- Peak query mix: 70% short lookups (50-300 tokens), 30% long generative summaries (400-2,000 tokens)
- Expected steady-state volume: ~12M tokens/day (roughly 360M tokens/month) with bursts to 20M tokens/day during onboarding
- Latency SLO: 200–300ms for lookups, 1.2s for generative flows

What we took away re: caching: prefix caching for the short lookups is your biggest lever — you already have a lot of repeated prompts+templates coming from the field (same diagnostics prompts + device metadata). You suggested a conservative initial cache coverage target of ~30–40% of lookup queries.

Ask / next steps from our side:
1) Can you confirm the monthly token volume range we should use for the proposal (best/expected/worst)? We logged 200M / 360M / 600M as a working range — confirm if that aligns.
2) Agree on a pilot scope for the first 30 days (we recommend focusing the prefix cache on the top 500 unique lookup templates).
3) We'll produce a unit-econ table showing effective $/1M tokens under three cache hit-rate scenarios (conservative 20%, expected 35%, optimistic 55%) and include a recommended Dedicated capacity sizing for predictable latency.

I'll have Marissa attach the scenario workbook and a proposal draft. We recommend evaluating the expected 35% hit-rate case for budgeting purposes; optimistic numbers are helpful for long-term ROI conversations.

Thanks — talk soon,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachment: (see redwood_pricing_scenarios.xlsx, acme_proposal_draft.pdf)

From: Sophie Green <sophie@acmetherm.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmetherm.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 08:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cache coverage, hit-rate scenarios & target unit economics

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the ranges you listed look correct to me:
- Best: ~200M tokens/mo (early pilot limited scope)
- Expected: ~360M tokens/mo (field rollout month 2–3)
- Worst (full fleet + heavy telemetry): ~600M tokens/mo

On cache coverage: the 30–40% initial target is realistic. A couple of clarifications:
- Our long-form summaries are generally unique per device session and won't hit prefix cache; count those as non-cacheable for planning.
- The lookup templates are fairly templated — if you can cache the first 3–4 tokens of the prompt + standardized device context, we should get to ~35% quickly.

One important constraint on pricing: we have an internal procurement target of keeping tooling ops to under $75k/month in steady state for the assistant piece (excluding storage and infra). That gives us a hard constraint when you show effective $/1M.

Happy to run the pilot but procurement will need clear scenarios that show how caching moves us below the internal target.

— Sophie
Head of Product, Acme Thermal

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Green <sophie@acmetherm.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cache coverage, hit-rate scenarios & target unit economics

Hi Sophie —

Uploading the quick scenario workbook (attached). Below is the distilled effective unit-econ table we discussed. Numbers are illustrative and based on Redwood's hosted pricing baseline for the model tier we demoed (base compute cost assumptions only; discounts for Dedicated/reserved capacity not applied unless we size Dedicated).

Assumptions (baseline):
- Raw model price: $120 per 1M tokens (hosted list price for chosen model tier)
- Monthly token bands (expected): 360M tokens
- Prefix cache applies mainly to lookup queries which are ~70% of volume; of those, we can cache ~60% of the repeatable portion by templating the prompt (i.e., cacheable fraction of total tokens = 0.7 * 0.6 = 0.42)

Scenario math (effective cost per 1M tokens billed to you after cache savings):
1) Conservative (20% hit-rate on cacheable fraction):
   - Effective reduction = cacheable_fraction * hit_rate = 0.42 * 0.20 = 8.4% token savings
   - Effective cost = $120 * (1 - 0.084) = $109.92 per 1M tokens
2) Expected (35% hit-rate):
   - Effective reduction = 0.42 * 0.35 = 14.7%
   - Effective cost = $120 * (1 - 0.147) = $102.34 per 1M tokens
3) Optimistic (55% hit-rate):
   - Effective reduction = 0.42 * 0.55 = 23.1%
   - Effective cost = $120 * (1 - 0.231) = $92.28 per 1M tokens

If we apply those to your expected 360M tokens/month:
- Conservative: monthly model spend ≈ $39,571
- Expected: monthly model spend ≈ $36,842
- Optimistic: monthly model spend ≈ $33,221

Notes and caveats:
- These calculations assume token billing reduces linearly with cache hits (for prefix caching we deduct tokens avoided on model execution). For session-level caching (full response reuse) savings would be larger but less consistent across flows.
- Dedicated capacity reserved discounts materially lower $/1M — if Acme commits to a 12-month reserved baseline at 400M+/mo we can run precise Dedicated pricing; I'll add a reserved versus hosted sheet in the workbook.
- Implementation risk: initial hit rates are lower; we recommend a short A/B to measure real-world hit-rate (we can instrument per-template hit metrics).

Attachment: redwood_pricing_scenarios.xlsx — includes a tab that lets you toggle cacheable fraction and hit rates to produce a customized effective $/1M and monthly totals.

If procurement needs to see a path under $75k/month, the expected-case ($36.8k/month) keeps the model portion well below that — leaving room for storage/infra. If you want finance-friendly numbers, we can show a blended estimate including storage and a 10% buffer for burst traffic.

Next proposed steps:
- Karthik to confirm volume band for proposal (you flagged 360M expected).
- Run a 30-day pilot for top-500 templates with instrumentation (we’ll estimate incremental engineering time and include an SOW).
- If pilot meets >=35% hit-rate on cacheable fraction, we put together a Dedicated sizing + 12-month reserved pricing sheet.

— Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: cache coverage, hit-rate scenarios & target unit economics

Got it — thanks Sophie + Marissa.

Sophie: please confirm 1) that 360M tokens/mo is the expected baseline for budgeting and 2) procurement allowance you mentioned is $75k/month for assistant tooling. Once you confirm I'll:
- Share a one-page pilot SOW (top-500 templates, instrumentation, 30-day metrics)
- Send the formal proposal with the expected-case numbers and an optimistic path to procurement showing Dedicated reserved pricing that gets even lower than the optimistic hosted numbers

If procurement needs a target effective unit price to anchor negotiations, is $95/1M tokens a reasonable target for you (that sits between expected and optimistic scenarios and would give room under the $75k/month cap at ~360M/mo)? If yes, I’ll make that the target for the procurement slide.

Quick answers to your questions:
- Confirmed monthly band: 200M / 360M / 600M (use 360M for the proposal).
- We'll send the SOW and proposal by EOD Monday — Marissa is adding the reserved capacity workbook so you can see the Dedicated delta.

Thanks — Karthik
